title: Evaluating the Use of Large Language Models as Synthetic Social Agents in Social Science Research

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing literature and proposing independence checks such as shuffling prompt order and list placement to reveal artifacts in LLM-as-a-judge evaluations.
Reviewing vulnerabilities in LLM-as-a-judge pipelines where models exhibit systematic preferences based on response length.
Analyzing evaluation pipelines where LLMs show a bias toward their own generated outputs in judge settings.
Assessing algorithmic fidelity and subgroup calibration by analyzing bias gaps and predictive failures in gender-sensitive field experiments and survey replications.
Evaluating subgroup predictions and bias gaps across racial and ethnic groups compared to human survey baselines to measure demographic representation.
Comparing synthetic survey responses to human baselines (like the General Social Survey) to evaluate bias gaps across political groups.
